newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares may need pause before new DAX gains.
newsitem.headline: German shares may need pause before new DAX gains.

text.p: Germany's DAX index was closing in on the crucial 4,000-point level in post-bourse IBIS dealings on Monday but some traders said a pause may be necessary before future gains and a run to fresh record levels.
The IBIS DAX was up 46.58 points at 3,993.31 points and well above the bourse closing level when the DAX ended up 30.31 points at 3,972.84 points.
The firmer dollar, which has underpinned export-sensitive shares, has been the main engine for the market's advance.
But some traders said the market's heady rise of about 250 points since June 23 means it's time for a break.
"I'm surprised the market is still going so strong," said one Frankfurt dealer. "The underlying tone is still OK but the volumes to support these levels is not there."
"We need to gather some fresh momentum before 4,000 points can be maintained," he said of the DAX index. "That may mean pulling back to about 3,900 points and then make a run."

But others said the market was still fundamentally sound and that the DAX index would break the 4,000-point level later in the day, in part due to anticipated early gains on Wall Street on buying after last Thursday's record close.

"I think we can still break 4,000 points today," said one dealer. "Both the fundamental and technical factors are very supportive since the dollar is strong, there's no inflation worries and trading interest in the market is still buoyant."
The DAX made many attempts in post-bourse IBIS trade to break 4,000 points but failed to move above a lifetime high set at 3,997.55 points.
A main focal point of dealings was the start of trading in television network group ProSieben AG, whose shares were listed on the Frankfurt bourse on Monday.
ProSieben shares began trade at 87 marks, well above the issue price at 72 marks due to the shares being 50 times oversubscribed, and jumped to the closing price of 95 marks.
But the closing price was below a grey market quote of 106.00 to 110.00 marks seen early on Monday.
Retailer Metro AG was also a feature. Its shares jumped 9.40 marks to 205.50 on news it was in talks to acquire the Makro cash and carry business from SHV Holdings.
Sportswear group Puma AG was a top gainer, rising six percent to 52.50 marks, while software group SAP AG rose 15.30 marks to 398.80 marks.
